key_insight: A detonation-sprayed FeNiCoMoW coating increased AISI 321 stainless steel indentation hardness while reducing the retained-depth fraction, indicating greater depth recovery during unloading.
engineering_relevance: The coating offers a harder surface, while depth-based descriptors help distinguish its indentation recovery behavior from that of untreated steel.
method: Instrumented Vickers indentation measured maximum and residual depths.
Calculated Martens hardness HM, residual-depth-based Hpl, and Hpl/HM.
Optical microscopy assessed morphology; X-ray diffraction identified phases.
evidence_signal: The 145 ± 8 μm coating increased indentation hardness from 2.3 ± 0.17 to 8.65 ± 1 GPa, reduced the retained-depth fraction from 0.906 to 0.788, and increased Hpl/HM from 1.22 to 1.61.
watch_item: Indentation results alone do not establish coating adhesion, wear resistance, or service durability; Hpl should not be conflated with conventional contact-depth-based hardness.
paper_title: Indentation Evaluation of Elastic–Plastic Response and Surface Modifications in Stainless Steel
